500 g anchovies (cleaned): 2 cups cornmeal
1 bunch chard or black cabbage
Wash the anchovies well and chop finely.
Finely chop the onion and greens.
Knead the cornmeal, vegetables, anchovies, olive oil, salt and hot water into a soft mixture.
Spread 2 cm thick in a greased tray.
Bake in a 190 °C oven for 40–45 minutes until the top is golden.
Head and trotter soup (kelle paça)
2 cleaned lamb’s trotters
1 lamb’s head (cleaned)
To serve: 3 garlic cloves, half a cup vinegar, 1 dessert spoon salt
Wash the trotters and head in cold water and boil in plenty of water, skimming the foam, for 3–4 hours (1.5 hours in a pressure cooker).
Take the meat off the bones, shred it and strain the stock.
Toast the flour in butter and stir in the stock until smooth.
Add the meat, boil for 10 minutes and add salt.
Thicken with egg yolk and lemon; serve with garlic vinegar.
Buy the product cleaned, from a trustworthy butcher.
Homemade sushi rolls (with cooked ingredients)
1.5 cups sushi rice
2 tablespoons rice vinegar
4 nori sheets
150 g cooked prawns or smoked salmon
4 tablespoons soy sauce
Wash the rice until the water runs clear; bring to the boil with 1.8 cups water, cook over a low heat for 12 minutes and leave to steam for 10 minutes.
Dissolve the vinegar, sugar and salt and mix into the hot rice; cool to room temperature.
Cut the cucumber, carrot and avocado into thin sticks.
Place the nori on the bamboo mat; with wet hands, spread the rice thinly, leaving a 2 cm gap at the top edge.
Arrange the vegetables and prawns along the bottom edge and roll up tightly with the mat.
Cut into 8 pieces with a wet knife and serve with soy sauce.
Cooked prawns or smoked products are used because raw fish is not recommended in pregnancy.
Chicken tacos
8 small corn or wheat tortillas
1 dessert spoon ground red pepper
Half a bunch coriander or parsley
Cut the chicken into strips, toss with the spices and salt and cook in a little oil for 8 minutes.
Finely chop the tomato, onion and coriander and make a salsa with lemon and salt.
Mash the avocado and mix with lemon and salt.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 30 seconds on each side.
Fill the tortillas with chicken, salsa, avocado and a spoonful of yogurt, fold and serve.
Chicken ramen
2 portions ramen noodles
1 dessert spoon sesame oil
Boil the eggs for 7 minutes, transfer to cold water and peel.
Boil the chicken stock with garlic, ginger and soy sauce for 10 minutes.
Cook the chicken in the broth for 15 minutes, remove and slice.
Boil the noodles separately for the time on the packet and drain.
Add the spinach to the hot broth and cook for 1 minute.
Put noodles, chicken and spinach in bowls and pour over the hot broth; serve with half an egg, spring onion and sesame oil.
Breakfast poğaça (cheese buns)
For the filling: 200 g white cheese, half a bunch parsley
Mix the milk, oil, egg white, yeast, sugar and salt; knead into a soft dough, adding the flour little by little.
Leave the dough to rise for 40 minutes.
Pull off walnut-sized pieces, flatten in your hand, add the cheese filling and close.
Arrange on the tray, brush with egg yolk and leave for 15 more minutes.
Bake in a 190 °C oven for 25 minutes until golden on top.
Lokma (fried dough balls in syrup)
For the syrup: 2 cups sugar, 2 cups water, a few drops of lemon
Boil the syrup for 10 minutes, add the lemon and cool.
Whisk the flour, yeast, sugar, salt and water into a runny batter; leave to rise for 45 minutes.
Squeeze the batter out through your fist, cut off with a wet spoon and drop into the hot oil.
Fry for 3–4 minutes, turning, until golden.
Drop the fried lokma into the cold syrup, leave for 1 minute and remove.
Beef tantuni (Mersin style)
500 g beef leg (cut into very thin strips)
2 tablespoons cottonseed oil
To serve: 2 tomatoes, 1 onion, parsley, sumac, lemon
Boil the meat in lightly salted water for 10 minutes and drain.
Heat the oil in a wide pan, add the meat and sauté with chilli flakes and a little cooking water for 10 minutes.
Finely chop the tomato, onion and parsley and mix with sumac.
Press the lavash into the oil in the pan to warm it; add the meat and salad and roll up.
Kalburabastı (patterned syrup cookies)
1 cup walnut kernels
Syrup: 3 cups sugar, 3 cups water, half a lemon
Boil the syrup for 15 minutes, add the lemon and cool.
Mix the oil, yogurt, egg and baking powder; knead into a soft dough, adding the flour little by little.
Flatten walnut-sized pieces, put walnuts inside and shape into ovals.
Press onto a sieve or grater to make a pattern and arrange on the tray.
Bake in a 180 °C oven for 30 minutes until golden.
The pattern helps the syrup soak in better.
Saray sarması (palace rolls)
10 sheets baklava pastry
2 cups coarsely ground walnuts
Syrup: 2.5 cups sugar, 2 cups water, half a lemon
Brush butter between two sheets, stack them and sprinkle with walnuts.
Roll around a thin rolling pin, scrunch from both ends and pull out the pin.
Cut the scrunched rolls into 4 cm pieces, arrange on the tray and drizzle with melted butter.
Bake in a 180 °C oven for 35 minutes.
Pour the cold syrup over while hot.
Scrunching creates the dessert’s crisp layers.
Stuffed kadayıf rolls
150 g butter
Make the syrup and let it cool.
Toss the kadayıf with melted butter.
Spread a pinch of kadayıf on your palm, put walnuts in the middle and roll up.
Arrange tightly on the tray.
Kadayıf breaks if it dries out; keep it covered while you work.
Katmer (Antep style)
Dough for 1 sheet (250 g flour, water, salt)
3 tablespoons ground pistachios
3 tablespoons kaymak
2 tablespoons granulated sugar
Knead the dough and rest for 20 minutes.
Brushing with butter, roll it out paper-thin.
Put kaymak, pistachios and sugar in the middle and fold the four sides over like an envelope.
Cook for 3–4 minutes on each side in a preheated 220 °C oven or on a sac griddle.
Slice while hot and serve.
In Antep it is eaten at breakfast.
Hot, straight away.
Lor cheese dessert
500 g lor cheese
Grated zest of 1 lemon
Syrup: 2 cups sugar, 2.5 cups water
Whisk the lor cheese, eggs and sugar until smooth.
Add the semolina, baking powder and lemon zest.
Bake in a greased tin in a 180 °C oven for 35 minutes.
Slice while hot and pour over the cold syrup.
Keeping the syrup light brings out the flavour of the lor cheese.

3.5 cups flour
